title: Heritage demolition decisions at short planning meeting
subtitle: Two heritage property items passed on consent, four by-laws approved, and the meeting ended within minutes.
overview: Council's May planning meeting was brief, chaired by a councillor because the mayor was absent. Two heritage items were handled together on the consent agenda, with no one asking to pull either for separate discussion {{vote:m1}}.

At 2187 Gordon Street, Council refused an application to demolish cultural heritage resources because the property is already protected by a heritage designation by-law under the Ontario Heritage Act {{vote:m2}}. This means the protected buildings cannot be demolished under that application.

At 9 Omar Street, Council removed the property from the Municipal Register of Cultural Heritage Properties and approved demolition of the dwelling {{vote:m3}}. The register lists properties of potential heritage value, so removal lets the demolition go ahead.
Council also approved four by-laws as amended {{vote:m4}}. There were no disclosures of pecuniary interest, and the meeting adjourned at 6:05 p.m.

decisions.detail: Council refused the application to demolish the cultural heritage resources because the property is protected by heritage designation By-law (2024)-20901 under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act.
Council removed 9 Omar Street from the Municipal Register of Cultural Heritage Properties and approved demolition of the dwelling.

debate: No debate took place on the consent items: the chair asked whether anyone wanted either heritage item pulled for discussion, and no one did.
The by-laws were moved, seconded and passed with no questions or opposition recorded in the transcript.
